primary_claim: Phrase Nudging, a decode-time steering technique that uses Bhattacharyya-coefficient-based SLERP interpolation toward clustered target 'phrase' distributions, can qualitatively steer a small LLM's generated reasoning trace toward the vocabulary and themes of a chosen phrase cluster while remaining mostly coherent.
stated_future_work: Improve evidence quality by learning about older NLP techniques that don't rely on backpropagation
Attempt to demonstrate a quantitative difference between baseline and phrase-nudged LLM token streams
Dedicate the next few months to a deep dive, developing this into a series of posts
limitations_stated: The process isn't perfect; nudged outputs contain a few misplaced tokens
Results presented are qualitative and functionally anecdotal so far, not yet quantitatively validated
quote: Notice how the nudged LLM acts similar to the phrases its being pushed towards while still maintaining coherent and relevant speech.
